title: Product video organization profile
description: Everything the product-video engine needs to know about one organization: brand, the apps to record, the environment where recording is safe, and the creative decisions that are already settled. Secrets never go in this file; name the environment variables that hold them.

tagline.description: One line for the end card of a hype cut.

windowTitle.description: Text in the browser frame's title pill. Defaults to the product name.

accent.description: Highlights: cursor ring, callouts, accent words, glow.

dark.description: Dark text and the backdrop behind framed phone shots.

stage.description: Near-black stage of the hype cut. Defaults to #060706.

heading.description: Font family name. A Google Fonts family (e.g. "Montserrat") loads by name; any other needs files in fontFiles.

body.description: Font family name, as for heading.

logo.description: Image path relative to this file (PNG or SVG on a transparent background). Without one, cards show the product name as text.

fontFiles.description: Font files for families that are not on Google Fonts. The organization must hold the licence to use them in video.

path.description: woff2, woff, ttf or otf, relative to this file.

baseUrl.description: Where the web app is recorded. Its host must be listed in environment.allowedHosts.

viewport.description: Recording viewport for narrated shots. Default 1920x1080.

stillViewport.description: Viewport for 2x stills and screencasts in the hype cut. Default 1440x900.

hideCss.description: CSS injected into every page to hide dev overlays, chat widgets or banners.

probePaths.description: Paths the probe visits to save a screenshot and an accessibility snapshot of each page.

auth.description: How the recorder signs in. Credentials are read from the named environment variables at run time.

path.description: A Playwright storage-state file a person created by signing in once. Keep it out of version control.

url.description: Login endpoint, absolute or relative to baseUrl.

body.description: JSON body. A value of the form "env:NAME" is replaced with that environment variable.

submit.description: Accessible name of the submit button.

waitFor.description: Path the app lands on after signing in.

appId.description: Bundle identifier of the build installed on the simulator.

screen.description: Pixel size of the simulator's screen recording, e.g. 1206x2622.

readyWhen.description: What the signed-in start screen shows; every shot waits for it after relaunch. Give an id or a text.

signIn.description: How the test account gets signed in: a flow file path or a sentence for the operator.

cleanupFlows.description: Maestro flows that must run at the end of every session to remove anything a recording created.

environment.description: The one place recording is allowed. The recorder refuses to start anywhere else.

kind.description: "live" is a real account on the real app: it is only accepted together with safety.readOnly.

description.description: What makes this environment safe: whose data it holds and how it is reset.

allowedHosts.description: Hosts (with port) the recorder may open, e.g. localhost:3000.

forbiddenHosts.description: Production hosts. Any request to one is aborted.

services.description: Local processes to start before recording.

readyUrl.description: Answers 2xx or 3xx once the service is up.

neverDo.description: Actions that must never happen while recording, in plain words: "send a message", "confirm a payment".

mask.description: What must never be readable on screen: "customer names", "email addresses".

blockRequests.description: Network backstop for the web recorder: matching requests are aborted.

readOnly.description: Abort every request that is not a read (anything but GET, HEAD or OPTIONS) once the recorder has signed in. Required when environment.kind is "live". WebSocket messages are not covered.

readOnlyAllow.description: Requests read-only mode lets through because the app uses them to read data, e.g. a GraphQL query endpoint. Add one only after checking it cannot change anything.

mode.description: silent: no voice. system: the operating system's voice, for timing or as final. command: your own text-to-speech command. recorded: a person supplies the files.

command.description: Shell command for mode "command". It reads the text from the file in $VO_TEXT_FILE and writes audio to $VO_OUT.

pointOfView.description: Who is speaking, e.g. "third person; never the founder's own voice".

pronunciations.description: Spellings to speak differently: { "FAQs": "F A Qs" }.

bpm.description: Tempo the hype cut is edited on.

handoff.description: Who receives the finished file and what must not happen to it, e.g. "send to the requester only; never upload or post".

delivery.description: The edit is laid out for 1920x1080 at 30 fps; these settings cover the delivery file.

decisions.description: Creative and wording decisions that are already settled. The agent applies them without asking again.
